A1.justification: Both PDFs describe C-PGC and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Visual inspection resolves extraction difficulties, and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 Sections 5–6 and appendices report original retrieval, captioning, grounding, entailment, LVLM-transfer, ablation, and defense experiments.

after.justification: V2 Section 4 and Appendices D–G report original benchmark results, ablations, feature-distance measurements, and qualitative attack examples.

M1.justification: V1 Section 4.3 and Algorithm 1 select individual texts with Top-K feature distances; v2 Section 3.3 and Algorithm 1 select the farthest text-description set. This revises the reported positive-sample procedure. The generator architecture, loss components, and token-replacement strategy remain substantially unchanged.

E1.justification: The four datasets and retrieval, captioning, grounding, and entailment tasks remain, including cross-domain retrieval. However, v1 Section 5.4/Table 6's prompted image-text correspondence tests on Qwen-VL, VisualGLM, LLaVA, and MiniGPT-4 disappear entirely, substantially narrowing evaluation scenarios.

E2.justification: V1 Table 2 evaluates SGA and TMM against C-PGC on Flickr30K; v2 removes this comparison entirely, substantially narrowing comparisons with contemporary multimodal attacks. GAP remains the principal benchmark baseline, and UAP/GAP remain in the motivational comparison.

E3.justification: Principal splits, training sample counts, epochs, and perturbation budgets remain unchanged as reported. V2 introduces a 5,000-pair feature-distance evaluation and an image-only control, replaces the averaged-embedding positive control with random positives, and omits CLIPViT from the perturbation-budget plots.

E4.justification: V2 adds direct alignment-distance analysis, a text-perturbation omission ablation, and grounding/entailment case studies. It removes v1's no-generator ablation and replaces the averaged-positive control with random positives. Defense, cross-domain, loss-component, and hyperparameter analyses remain, despite substantial relocation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed identifiers, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. V2's augmentation-noise parameters and averaged feature-distance results do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Many corresponding results change: Table 1 reports Flickr30K ALBEF-to-BLIP text-retrieval ASR as 72.13% in v1 and 44.79% in v2. Captioning, grounding, defense, cross-domain, and R@5/R@10 scores also change, alongside added diagnostics and deleted comparisons. Changed clean-model baselines preclude interpreting all differences as controlled performance gains or losses.

T1.justification: V2 Appendix D introduces the relative cross-modal feature-distance definition in Equation 6. Its additional attack-goal and constrained-objective equations largely formalize existing content; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: V2 retains the universal multimodal attack contribution but withdraws prominent claims of surpassing instance-specific SGA/TMM attacks and transferring successfully to LVLMs. It also drops the explicit first-to-exploit-both-modalities priority claim, substantially narrowing the claimed contribution.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretation of the separate benefits of image-only attacks and textual perturbations. It removes explanations asserting generator dominance and linking LVLM robustness to language ability or model size. The principal alignment mechanism, perturbation-interaction limitation, semantic-inconsistency caveat, and SNLI-VE annotation warning remain.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-repository link, temperature 0.1, Gaussian augmentation mean 0 and standard deviation 0.5, and averaging of caption embeddings for conditioning. These are newly disclosed details. Conversely, v1's explicit CLIP ViT-B/16 and ResNet-101 backbone specifications are omitted.

R1.justification: V2 substantially prunes v1's VLP background and general attack/defense literature, including discussion of downstream-agnostic generative attacks. It adds references including Gao et al. (2024), Anil et al. (2024), and Wang et al. (2023), while removing explicit first-in-field positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, background and related work are consolidated, and the standalone threat-model section disappears. Defenses move into evaluation, while dataset descriptions, training details, and limitations are redistributed into appendices. This substantially changes the narrative structure.

P2.justification: The layout changes from two columns to one. V2 rearranges introductory figures, transposes the grounding table, merges cross-domain tables and perturbation-budget plots, and adds diagnostic tables and two visualization figures. The SGA/TMM and LVLM tables disappear. Some revised captions misdescribe their displays, notably Table 5's claim of averaged results.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful alignment evidence, an image-only ablation, and reproducibility details. Its narrower claims accompany removal of substantial comparison and transfer evidence, including the generator ablation. Many results change without explaining their provenance, and new caption inconsistencies weaken clarity. These benefits and losses do not establish a reliable net quality direction from the PDFs alone.
